lessons.title: Lesson 1: Dining etiquette and table manners around the world
objectives: Nắm vững các khái niệm và định nghĩa cốt lõi của Lesson 1: Dining etiquette and table manners around the world.
Hiểu và áp dụng thành thạo các quy tắc và công thức trong SGK.
Rèn luyện kỹ năng phân tích và giải quyết các bài toán/tình huống thực tiễn.

concepts.definition: 'Must' expresses internal obligation from the speaker's own feelings or moral sense; 'Have to' expresses external obligation from rules, laws, or circumstances.
concepts.example: I must call my grandmother today. (My personal wish) / You have to wear a uniform at school. (School rule)
concepts.essence: In the past tense, 'had to' must be used because 'must' has no past form.

rules.meaning: 'Mustn't' means you are NOT allowed to do it (forbidden); 'Don't have to' means it is NOT necessary (you can do it if you want).
rules.example: You mustn't speak loudly in the library. / Tomorrow is Sunday, so I don't have to wake up early.
rules.essence: Crucial distinction between prohibition and freedom of choice.

workedExamples.prompt: Choose 'mustn't' or 'don't have to': 'You __________ touch the temple statues; it is strictly forbidden.'
steps: Step 1: 'strictly forbidden' signals a strict legal/religious prohibition.
Step 2: 'Mustn't' is the modal verb of strict prohibition.
Step 3: Complete sentence: 'You mustn't touch the temple statues; it is strictly forbidden.'

commonMistakes.mistake: Using 'mustn't' when you want to say something is unnecessary.
commonMistakes.why: If something is not needed, use 'don't have to' or 'needn't'. 'Mustn't' means DO NOT DO IT UNDER ANY CIRCUMSTANCES.
